title: Small-batch release runner + locality-aware throttle plan (April 2027) - draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc defines a small-batch rollout runner for the upcoming model-serving change (kv-cache invalidation + kernel selector tweak) and a locality-aware throttle curve. Primary goals: minimize user-visible error surface, keep tail latency SLOs, and provide a rapid rollback path if quality regressions appear.

Context and motivation:
- Recent kernel selector improvement reduces throughput variance for long-context streams but requires a short-lived KV cache reset to pick up new cache-sharding metadata.
- Full rollout risks bursty cold starts in specific regions (APAC east-west replication windows).
- We need to exercise variant routing and locality throttles so customers on Dedicated/Private get graceful degradation rather than abrupt failures.

High-level approach:
1) Small-batch runner: progressive batches of clients/users (not full traffic) using a job that increments cohort percentage by route and by region. Batches are defined by customer_id hash buckets to ensure deterministic partial coverage.
2) Locality-aware throttle: when a region shows elevated cold-starts or latency, the runner will reduce concurrency and increase batching for that region only; fallback to nearby region variants as a last resort.
3) Observability: preflight probes, smoke set, and a quality guard defined by eval prompt set. If quality or latency thresholds are breached, runner pauses and triggers investigator alerts.

Schedule (calendar overview):
- T-7 days (2027-04-09): Finalize cohort lists and update canary job config. Post canary config PR. Notify SRE and oncall.
- T-3 days (2027-04-13): Run dry-run on staging with synthetic traffic and KV reset simulation. Collect baseline telemetry.
- T-1 day (2027-04-15): Preflight probes against production test endpoints, validate smoke set (10 prompts), warm caches. Night window reserved 00:00-04:00 PT.
- D-day (2027-04-16): Start batch 0 (0.5% traffic) 02:00 PT, monitor 60m. If green, advance every 90m to next batch sizes: 0.5 -> 1 -> 2 -> 5 -> 10 (per-region caps). Full roll at 12h if stable.
- Post-roll (up to T+72h): Slow ramp to all routes; maintain elevated telemetry sampling and run regression evals at 6h/24h/48h.

Batching and cohort sizing (default):
- Batch 0: 0.5% global, max 1% per-region cap
- Batch 1: 1% global, max 2% per-region cap
- Batch 2: 2% global, max 4% per-region cap
- Batch 3: 5% global, max 8% per-region cap
- Batch 4: 10% global, max 15% per-region cap
Notes: These are conservative defaults for long-sequence models. For low-latency chat routes we may double pacing.

Locality-aware throttle rules (runtime):
- Trigger conditions (any of): regional p95 latency > baseline_p95 * 1.25 for > 5m, regional errors > baseline_errors + 0.5% absolute for > 2m, or cache-miss spike > baseline_miss_rate * 2.
- On trigger: reduce concurrency cap by 30% for region, increase batching target by +20% for incoming requests in that region for 10m, and route new requests to nearest healthy region variant if latency > baseline_p95*1.4 for > 60s.
- Escalation: if region still failing after 30m, pause advance and notify Release Conductor + SRE lead; run manual canary rollback for region.

Preflight and smoke checklist (what to run):
- [ ] Ensure canary job has the right hash bucketing file in /deploy/buckets/2027-04-16
- [ ] Update canary config PR and get +1 from eng-release-engineering and eng-sre
- [ ] Run staging KV-reset simulation and confirm no increased tail latency beyond 10%
- [ ] Smoke set (owner: Priya) run results uploaded to internal S3: s3://redwood-internal/release-smoke/2027-04-16
- [ ] Update Ops Pager rotation for 24h (weekend watch) and add extra liaison to #release-ops

Telemetry probes and dashboards to watch (quick list):
- p50/p95/p99 latency by region, by route
- token/sec throughput and GPU utilization across Dedicated pools
- cache-hit ratio and cold-starts per host
- eval regressions: BLEU-style delta and semantic-sim drift on the smoke set
- error types: 5xx vs validation-errors vs quota-failures
- rollout job health: success/failure count for cohort advances in the runner
Linked dashboards: (add to PR description)

Rollback and fallback playbook (concise):
1) Immediate rollback: pause runner and flip routing to previous model variant (model:v2027-03-29) for cohorts still on new runtime. This is a fast toggle in the routing service (2-3s).
2) Warmback: if rollback happens due to cache invalidation problems, perform a controlled KV reseed + slowwarm (20% of nodes warmed per 10m) before attempting re-roll.
3) If rollback cannot be performed quickly (routing control-plane issue), then throttle traffic globally to preserve SLOs and open incident with SRE.
4) Post-incident: capture snapshots (perf traces, kernel selection logs) and open RE-incident ticket with triage notes.

Release notes — draft (to be refined for public-facing changelog):
Title: Kernel selector stability improvements and KV cache sharding fix (April 2027)
Notable changes:
- Improved kernel selection logic to reduce throughput variance on long-context workloads (internal perf +18% median for sequences > 8k).
- Corrected cache-shard metadata update path to prevent stale KV lookups during model variant swap.
- Minor telemetry labels added for regional cache-miss signal.
Known caveats / limitations:
- Short window of elevated cold-starts may occur immediately after cohort advances in a few APAC sub-regions while KV reseed finishes. We expect this to be transient (minutes) and mitigated by locality throttles.
- Older Dedicated reservations pinned to model:v2027-03-21 will not see the kernel selector change until they opt in or we migrate per contract.

Operational notes for customer-success and support:
- CS template for inbound requests (use this copy):
  "We deployed a small runtime change this morning to improve long-context throughput. If you are seeing occasional slower responses, we are likely running a controlled batch expansion in your region. Please share request IDs and timestamps and we will prioritize investigation"
- Escalation paths: RE oncall -> SRE lead -> Eng oncall -> Product PM. Add customer case IDs to RE-4821.

Runbook quick commands (ops cheatsheet):
- Pause rollout: curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/rollouts/pause -d '{"id":"kv-reset-2027-04"}' (ops-only)
- Rollback to previous variant: ./bin/route-toggle --model model:v2027-03-29 --target cohorts
- Increase sampling: ./telemetryctl sample --path smoke-set --rate 10x

Open questions and TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm APAC cold-start baseline numbers with infra (Diego) — still waiting for raw logs from 2027-03-28 night test.
- Decide whether to add a second fallback variant that uses more aggressive quantization to reduce tail latency for Dedicated customers. Tradeoff: potential quality degradation.
- Add a one-click KV-reseed utility to the ops toolkit to speed warmback.

Appendix: quick smoke prompts (owner: Priya)
1) Summarize: "Explain the difference between batching and caching in model serving."
2) Long-context: 12k-token passage plus question -> verify response stays coherent for last 1k tokens.
3) Latency probe: 40 concurrent chat requests with 1k token length window.

Notes history and edits:

- 2027-04-06 Michael: updated rollback commands and smoke-set link
